title: Independence of the integral representative
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, $X,Y$ finite-type $K_0$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\mathcal C_W=D^b_c(W,R)$ be the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and let $Q_W:\mathcal C_W\to\mathcal C_W[1/\varpi]=D^b_c(W,E)$ be its raw scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For any $K,K'\in\mathcal C_X$ and any specified isomorphism $\alpha:Q_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XK'$, the two rational compact-support images
$$
Q_Y(Rf_!K)=(Rf_!K)\otimes_R^L E,\qquad
Q_Y(Rf_!K')=(Rf_!K')\otimes_R^L E
$$
of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], interpreted using the coherent tower of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], have an induced isomorphism $\beta_\alpha:Q_Y(Rf_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_Y(Rf_!K')$, functorial in $\alpha$. It sends identities to identities and compositions to compositions. Equivalently, for specified presentations $a:Q_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ and $a':Q_XK'\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ of a common rational object, the canonical comparison is $\beta_{(a')^{-1}a}$. The word canonical refers to these specified identifications, not to a choice-independent isomorphism between bare isomorphism classes.

proof.text: By the nonemptiness assertion of [prop-compactification-refinement], a compactification exists under exactly the field, finite-type and separated hypotheses in force. Fix the compactification used to compute the integral operation, once for every level. Use the small site and coefficient universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] to obtain $\mathcal T_f^c$ with evaluations $\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{!,n}K_n$ and the prescribed transitions. Put $B_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $\mathcal A_Y=\operatorname{Mod}(B_Y)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] on a small representative of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, in the coefficient universes, to obtain the exact functor $L=R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A_Y))\to D(\mathcal A_Y)$. Its construction uses a K-injective resolution of the entire strict tower, rather than unrelated resolutions of its evaluations. Thus $F_f=L\mathcal T_f^c$ is a genuine exact functor, whose value is the integral derived-limit formula of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. No functoriality of arbitrary choices of cones in a triangulated category is invoked.

source.place: Proof first sentence, with the missing coherent tower distinguished from the derived-limit property; strict derived limit: Stacks Tag 0940, section-derived-limits (the cited tower-limit node supplies its module version).

proof.text: The functor $L$ is $R$-linear. The completed coefficient action of $a\in R$ on module sheaves is multiplication by its compatible constant sections, as specified by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear]; on a strict tower it is componentwise multiplication and commutes with every transition. The tower category is abelian by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Componentwise module identities make it $R$-linear, so [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] makes its derived localization $Q$ linear too. For a derived map $h:M\to N$, choose K-injective tower representatives $I_M,I_N$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Fix the resolution isomorphisms $q_M:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QI_M$ and $q_N:N\xrightarrow{\sim}QI_N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $q_Nh q_M^{-1}$ has a unique homotopy-class representative $\bar h:I_M\to I_N$. Since $Q$ and composition are linear, $Q(a\bar h)=aQ(\bar h)=q_N(ah)q_M^{-1}$; injectivity of the Hom map makes $a\bar h$ the representative of $ah$. For a second map $h':M\to N$, $Q(\bar h+\bar h')=Q(\bar h)+Q(\bar h')=q_N(h+h')q_M^{-1}$; the same injectivity makes $\bar h+\bar h'$ the representative of $h+h'$. Termwise inverse limit of compatible families satisfies $\lim(a\bar h)=a\lim(\bar h)$ and $\lim(\bar h+\bar h')=\lim(\bar h)+\lim(\bar h')$. Termwise limit also respects tower chain homotopies: a compatible degree $-1$ map $H$ with $u-v=dH+Hd$ gives $\lim u-\lim v=d(\lim H)+(\lim H)d$, by evaluating each component of a compatible family. Thus these calculations descend to homotopy classes. Applying the linear localization in the target proves both linearity identities for $L$. This does not require a scalar-linear choice of resolution functor. Since $\mathcal T_f^c$ is $R$-linear, so is $F_f$.

source.place: Proof first sentence, scalar-linearity supplied explicitly on K-injective tower representatives; derived Hom input Stacks Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; linear localization from the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: For every $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$, [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] applies to the same field, prime, coefficient field, compactification and transitions: every derived limit of this particular compact-support tower belongs to $D^b_c(Y,R)$, including the common cohomological interval required there. Thus $F_f$ restricts to the full integral constructible subcategories. Those subcategories have the induced triangulated structures by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] and the inherited linear structures by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear], so the restricted functor remains exact and $R$-linear. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] it is the integral operation $Rf_!$. This step uses a constructibility theorem, not the definition as evidence of its own preservation claim.

source.place: Proof first sentence: checking the integral functor lands in the stated full subcategory before rationalization; preservation is the existing constructibility node, with exactly its hypotheses.

proof.text: Write $F=F_f|_{D^b_c(X,R)}$. Using [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], define $F_E(K)=F(K)$ and $F_E(u\otimes e)=F(u)\otimes e$ on each rational Hom module. By [def-weil-module-base-change], $R$-linearity of $F$ makes this a well-defined $E$-linear Hom map: $F(ru)\otimes e=F(u)\otimes re$. For pure tensors, $F_E((v\otimes b)(u\otimes a))=F(vu)\otimes ba=(F(v)\otimes b)(F(u)\otimes a)$; bilinearity gives the identity for sums. Also $F_E(1_K\otimes1)=1_{F(K)}\otimes1$. Hence it is a functor. Any $E$-linear extension must send $u\otimes e=e(u\otimes1)$ to $e(F(u)\otimes1)$, proving uniqueness. This is the scalar-localization calculation of rational transport, performed on these actual Hom modules; it identifies neither the completed coefficient sheaf with a discrete constant sheaf nor two different definitions of an integral constructible category.

source.place: Proof, rational-transport sentence, expanded as its elementary tensor-Hom formula; tensor balancing: Stacks Tag 05G3, algebra-definition-base-change.

proof.text: Define $\beta_\alpha=F_E(\alpha)$ and its inverse to be $F_E(\alpha^{-1})$. Their composites are $F_E(\alpha^{-1}\alpha)=1$ and $F_E(\alpha\alpha^{-1})=1$, so this is the asserted isomorphism. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], $F_E$ on objects is precisely the displayed rational compact-support operation. If $a:Q_XK\to M$ and $a':Q_XK'\to M$ are the specified presentations, the input comparison is $(a')^{-1}a$, so the stated comparison is its image. For a third presentation $a''$, $(a'')^{-1}a'\,(a')^{-1}a=(a'')^{-1}a$; applying $F_E$ proves the cocycle. The identity presentation gives the identity and a composite of input isomorphisms gives the corresponding composite of comparisons. If one changes the presentations, their new relative isomorphism gives its own functorial comparison; no uniqueness of an isomorphism chosen from a bare existence assertion is claimed.

source.place: Proof final sentence: explicit images of an isomorphism and its inverse, with identity, composition, and presentation cocycle checks.
